blocks.c: One: the 1994 log ends in October 1994. Wen Aguilar's handwriting appears in every volume after it, up to and including this year.
Two: the front page of every volume has a staff list, and I checked all of them, and Wen Aguilar appears on exactly one — 1994, night technician, start date January, no end date.
So either a woman who left this building thirty-one years ago has been coming back to write in the margins of our maintenance logs.
Or she never left, and she has been writing in them the whole time, from wherever she is.
I looked at that for about an hour.

Then I got out this year's book and turned to the current page and wrote a question in it, in the margin, in the same place her notes always appear. I felt ridiculous doing it. It was three in the morning and I was writing a note to a building.
How do I get to minus three?
I closed the book. I did my 03:00 walk. Thirty-one landings. Nothing wrong except the north stair smell, which is worse in the spring, and the door closer on 22, which has been dying since Christmas.
I came back to the office at 03:40 and opened the book.
Under my question, in block capitals, in wet ink:
YOU DON'T. THE CAR ONLY GOES TO MINUS ONE.
IF YOU WANT TO GO DEEPER YOU HAVE TO BE INVITED, AND IT INVITES YOU BY TAKING SOMETHING SMALL FROM YOU AND SEEING WHETHER YOU NOTICE.
IT TOOK SOMETHING FROM YOU LAST NIGHT.
IF YOU CANNOT WORK OUT WHAT IT WAS BY THE END OF YOUR SHIFT, DO NOT COME BACK TO THIS BUILDING. — W.A.
